cards.explanation: The answer is obey, friends. God says, "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant…" (Jeremiah 11:3). Not just hear them, not just nod at them. Obey is the word that carries the whole message.

The answer is that they would be His people and He their God. God told them, "Obey Me, and do everything I command you, and you will be My people, and I will be your God." (Jeremiah 11:4). No prize list, just Him and His people together. That's about the best deal anybody ever got offered.

The answer is True. God says He was establishing "…the oath I swore to your forefathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey…" (Jeremiah 11:5). He made a promise and put an oath on it. And the verse adds that the land is theirs "…as it is to this day."

The answer is False, friends. God says, "…I strongly warned them again and again, saying, ‘Obey My voice.’" (Jeremiah 11:7). Again and again is a lot more than once, and it covers the time from Egypt until that day.

The answer is the stubbornness of his evil heart. The verse says, "…each one followed the stubbornness of his evil heart." (Jeremiah 11:8). They wouldn't obey or incline their ears, and that's what they followed instead. That's a hard one to read, friends.

The answer is True. God says, "So I brought on them all the curses of this covenant I had commanded them to follow but they did not keep." (Jeremiah 11:8). That's a heavy line. The verse says they did not keep the covenant, and the curses came.

The answer is True. God says, "They have returned to the sins of their forefathers who refused to obey My words." (Jeremiah 11:10). They went right back to what the forefathers did. That's a tough thing to hear.

The answer is the house of Israel and the house of Judah. God says, "The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers." (Jeremiah 11:10). Both houses are named. Nobody gets left out of that sentence.

The answer is to the gods they burn incense to. God says they "…will go and cry out to the gods to which they have been burning incense…" (Jeremiah 11:12). They head for the gods they've been serving. And the verse says right away that those gods will not save them.

The answer is False, friends. God says, "…these gods certainly will not save them in their time of disaster." (Jeremiah 11:12). The very gods they've been burning incense to will not save them. The verse says so plainly.

The answer is False. God says, "…do not pray for these people. Do not raise up a cry or a prayer on their behalf, for I will not be listening when they call out to Me in their time of disaster." (Jeremiah 11:14). That's a hard word for Jeremiah to carry.
The answer is True. God says, "When you are wicked, then you rejoice." (Jeremiah 11:15). I think it's a sad line. It's what God says about them in that verse.

The answer is that He will set it on fire. God says, "…with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed." (Jeremiah 11:16). The tree was once called beautiful, and that makes the fire a hard picture to look at.

The answer is planted, friends. The verse says, "The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you…" (Jeremiah 11:17). Planted is the exact word the verse uses. He's the one who put them in the ground, so the olive tree picture fits together.
